FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Part 2/See 80) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Electric Fans Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. This standard is to be read in conjunction with IS 302-1(1979) `Safety of household and similar electrical appliances: Part 1 General requirements'. For the sake of convenience, the clauses of this standard correspond to those of IS 302-1, instead of reproducing full text of each clause, clauses of IS 302-1 which are applicable (which means that relevant provisions of the clause apply) or not applicable and the sub clauses or portions thereof which are not applicable are indicated as under: a) b) In case of a clause where it is applicable or not applicable, the wording used is `This clause of IS 302-1 `is applicable/not applicable. In case of sub-clause or part thereof `Not applicable'. `Replacement � followed by the new text'. Any addition to the existing provisions of a sub-clause of IS 302- 1(1979) has been indicated as under: `Addition -- followed by the text of the additional matter'. Clauses/tables which are additional to those of IS 302-1 are numbered starting from 101 and additional subclauses are numbered with the main clauses number followed by 101, 102, etc, for example, 7.101. Should however, any deviation exist between IS 302-1 and this standard, the provisions of the latter shall apply. This standard is based on corresponding IEC publication IEC 60335-2-80, Ed 2.0 (2002) issued by the International `Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) with the following modifications: a) b) c) d) e) f) g) h) j) m) n) Additional definitions are added, `T' marking specified on fans working at temperature higher than 40"C, Additional clause on ratings specified, Starting of motor operated appliances have been incorporated, Tests for transient overvoltage test not covered since the test is presently not covered in IS 302-1, Temperature rise limits specified instead of making reference to IS 302-1, Static and dynamic load test for ceiling suspended fan blade brackets incorporated, Test specified for mechanical strength are more stringent, Conformity of stamping material and capacitors to relevant Indian Standards specified, Schedule of type, acceptance and routine tests incorporated, and Sampling plan and criteria for conformity for acceptance tests incorporated.

Wherever a sub-clause of IS 302-1 is to be replaced by a new text, it has been indicated as under:

With the publication of this standard IS 12155:1987 `Specification for general and safety requirements for fans and regulators for household and similar purposes' the requirements of which are covered by this standard shall be treated as withdrawn. This standard does not cover the performance requirements. Indian Standards which are necessary adjuncts to this standard are given in Annex AA. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 1S 2: 1%0 `Rules for rounding.off numerical values (revised'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Normal Load -- Operation of the appliances under

This standard deals with safety of electric fans for household and similar purposes, their rated voltage being-not more than 250 V for single-phase appliances and 415 V for other appliances.
NOTES 1 Examples of fans which are within the scope of this standard are: a) b) c) d) e) Ceiling fans; Table fans; Pedestal fans; Partition fans; and Duct fans (ventilating

the following conditions. Table and pedestal fans are operated oscillating mechanism in operation. Ceiling fans are fixed to a ceiling. Partition fans are installed in the centre of a suitable partition having dimensions at least four times the diameter of the air inlet. with any

fans). controls (regulators)

This standard also applies provided with the fans.

to separate

Fans not intended for normal household use but which nevertheless may be a source of danger to the public, such as, fans intended for use in shops, in light industry and on farms, are within the scope of this standard. So far as is practicable, this standard deals with the common hazards presented by appliances which are encountered by all persons in and around the home. This standard does not in general take into account: a) b) Use of appliances by young children or infirm persons without supervision; and Playing with the appliance by young children. For appliances intended to be used in vehicles or on board ships or aircraft, additional requirements may be necessary; and Additional requirements maybe specified by the national health authorities, the national authorities responsible for the protection of labour and similar authorities. Appliances purposes; intended exclusively for industrial

Duct fans are installed in a duct in accordance with the instructions for installation, the length of the duct being approximately four times the diameter of the fan.
Additional sub-clauses 2.101 Ceiling or Deck-Head Type Fan

A propeller-bladed fan having two or more blades and provided with a device for,suspension from the ceiling of a room so that the blades rotate in a horizontal plane.

2.102 Table or Cabin Type Fan A smaller-diameter propelldr-bladed fan having two or more blades and intended for use with free inlet and outlet of air. It maybe a table fan or bracket-mounted fan for wall or ceiling mounting. 2.103 Pedestal Type Fan A prQpeller type fan having two or more blades mounted on a pedestal of fixed or variable height and intended for use with free inlet and outlet of air driven by electric motors. 2.104 Blade Sweep The diameter of the circle traced out by the extreme tips of the fan blades. 2.105 Size af Fan The sweep in millimetres. 1

This standard does not cover performance requirement nor does it apply to household kitchen fans, air heaters required with fans, heating, ventilating units, mechanical refrigeration equipment or air conditioners.

This clause of IS 302-1 is applicable as follows. 7.2, 7.3.1 and 7.4 are not applicable. 7.12 Addition This instructions for installation shall state: a) Model or type reference of luminaires which may be installed in fans which are constructed for this purpose; b) For partition fans, if the fan is intended for mounting in outside windows or walls; c) For fans intended to be mounted at high level, that the fan is to be installed so that the blades are more than 2.3 m above the floor; and d) For duct and partition fans, that precautions must be taken to avoid the back-flow of gases into the room from the open flue of gas or other open-fire appliances.
11.1 Replacement

Fans shall not attain excessive temperature in normal use. Compliance is checked by determining the temperature rise of the various parts under the condit ions specified in relevant Indian Standards on electric fans.

20.103.1 A blade brackets used on a ceiling suspended

fan shall be subjected to the static load test-described in 20.103.2. 20.103.2 The mounting feet of the blade brackets shall be fixed by a support, vise or other securing means. The h-ackets shall be oriented as intended for actual use. After securing the bracket mounting feet, a crossbar is secured across the top of the outer-most blade mounting hole(s). The load is suspended from the centre of the crossbar for one minute. The combined weight of the crossbar, load and means of load suspension shall be in accordance with Table 1.02.

Additional Sub-clauses

20.-104 Dynamic

Load Test for Ceiling Suspended

Fan Blade 20.104.1 A blade bracket used on a ceiling suspended fan shall be subjected to the dynamic load test described in 20.104.2. 20.104.2 The fan blades and blade brackets are installed on the fan in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. The fan blade length and fan speed shall be considered so as to test the fan and blade combinations that will represent the most severe dynamic forces that can be induced by the 10 g imbalance described in 20.104.2.1.
20.104.2.1 A 10 g flat weight is secured to the fan blade that will result in the most change in the vertical distance of the blade imbalance. The weight is secured to the fan blade at the outermost point from the centre of the fan, but not on the edge of the fan blade.

22.24 to 22.27,22.29

22.101 Thermal cutouts, if any, incorporated in duct fans in order to comply with 19 shall be non-selfresetting. Compliance is checked by inspection. Fans having provision for attaching a luminaires shall incorporate appropriate terminals and internal wiring.
22.102

The fan is operated at maximum speed for 24 h. A reversible fan is to be operated in the upward airflow direction. After the test of 20.103 and 20.104, the fan brackets shall show no sign of cracks when visually examined by a 4-power magnifying glass.

creepage distances are specified shall not be located in air ducts unless adequate precautions are taken to reduce the effects of contamination. Compliance is checked by inspection.
NOTE -- This requirement is met if clearances are at least twice the values specified in 29.1 and for creepage distance-the insulation is suitable for extra-severe duty conditions according to 30.3.

be of adequate strength but maybe of the rigid or the non-rigid type, and shall comply with the following test. The suspension of the ceiling fan shall withstand a tensile load of 1000 kg witho{t breakage and a torsion load of 500 kg cm without breakage, Metal parts used in the suspension system shall have a minimum wall thickness of 1.5 mm. IS 302-2-80 (2003) 24 COMPONENTS This clause of IS 302-1 is applicable except as follows. 24.2 to 24.10 not applicable. 24.3 Addition Fans having a rated power input not exceeding 25 W may be fitted with a switch in the supply cord. 24.101 Stamping of fan motors shall be made from low loss electrical sheet steel conforming to IS 648 or any other suitable low loss electrical sheet steel. 24.102 Fans shall be fitted with two or more well balanced made from metal or other suitable material. The blades and motor shall be securely fixed so that they do not loose in operation. 24.103 Capacitors shall be easily replaceable and clearly marked with the maximum safe working temperature, and the corresponding voltage and capacitance. Capacitors shall comply with IS 1709. 24.104 Bearing shall be free from noise. Proper lubrication of bearings shall be carried out by the manufacturers.

101 TESTS 101.0 Tests are classified as type, acceptance and routine tests.

101.1 Type Test The tests specified in Table 103 shall constitute the type tests and shall be carried out on the selected samples of the same type and rating selected.preferably at random from a regular production lot (see 4.2). Before commencement of the tests, the sample shall be visually examined and inspected for obvious visual defects in respect of components, parts and their assembly, construction, mechanical hazards, markings, provision of suitable terminals for supply connections, earthing and the effectiveness of screws and connections. The external surface finish shall be even and free from finishing defects. 101.1.1 Criteria cfkceptance Sample shall successfully pass all the type tests for proving conformity with the requirements of the standard. 101.2 Acceptance Tests The tests specified in Table 104 shall constitute the acceptance tests: A recommended sampling procedure for acceptance tests is given in Annex.BB.

ANNEX (Clause RECOMMENDED BB

101.2.1)
SAMPLING PLAN

BB-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING BB-1.1 Lot

All fans along with associated regulator of the same type, grade, category and rating manufactured under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.
BB-1.2 The number to be selected from the lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 105. BB-1 .2.1 These fans shall be selected from the lot at random. In order to ensure randomness of selection, procedures given in IS 4905:1968 maybe followed.

BB-2 NUMBER

OF TESTS

AND CRITERIA

FOR CONFORMITY

according to COI 2 and 4 of Table 105 shall be subjected to the acceptance tests specified in 101.2.1. A fan failing to satisfy any of the acceptance tests shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements if the number of defective found in the sample is less than or equal to the acceptance number (see co] 6 of Table 105) and shall be rejected if it is greater than or equal to the rejection number (see CO17 of Table 105). If the number of defective lies between the acceptance number and rejection number, the second sample of the same size shall be chosen at random and tested. If the number of defective found in the combined samples is greater than or equal to the rejection number the lot shall be rejected, otherwise the lot shall be accepted.

BB-2.1 The fans at the first stage, selected at random

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. Review of Indidn Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
